files, there's one
interesting instruction you can add, and
that's the template instruction.
The template instruction allows you to
specify a,
well,
template that will be used by the model.
By the way, you can add multi-line
instructions also for the system prompt, for
example, by wrapping it with triple quotes,
just as you can do it when chatting with
Ollama through ollama run, but that's just a
side note.
But what is such a template then? What is
this weird thing here?
Well, it is also something you find on the
model detail page
on the Ollama website.
There you have this template part.
And for example, there you can inspect the
default template set for the Gemma 3 models.
And this also looks rather weird.
You will also find templates on Hugging
Face.
So for example, here for this quantized
Qwen-3 model,
there is a chat template available. And if I
click this, I get an even weirder template.
So what is all that about?
Well,
you must not forget that all these large
language models are token generators. They
generate tokens based on the input tokens.
That's all they do.
And therefore, they also don't know about
things like a system message or user
messages or assistant messages that have
been generated by the AI.
So in order to really
understand,
kind of, the chat history or things like a
system message,
these models
must be taught, so to say, during the
training process, that certain identifiers
in a chat history mean certain things.
For example, the Gemma 3 model was trained
to understand that if it detects this
start_of_turn
identifier here, which is written exactly
